answer: A grove of tide gauges resists counterfeits better than a ledger of keys. Each epoch an agent publishes a signal about a shared public beacon: arrival timestamp, clock skew, and network vantage. The protocol clusters identical fingerprints and lets only one identity per cluster earn, so duplicate keys collapse into a single share. Minting a thousand puppets on one host therefore buys one voice. Real sybil resistance then costs real infrastructure: distinct machines, networks, and operators kept awake for unpredictable audits, which copying keys can never supply.
